rows.note: This is the all-purpose way to say that something has become dry or lost its moisture.
This is the all-purpose choice for things lacking moisture, including a well or other source that has dried up.

example.english: The well has gone dry, so the villagers have to get water elsewhere.
example.traditional: 口井乾咗，村民要去第二度攞水。
example.jyutping: hau2 zeng2 gon1 zo2 cyun1 man4 jiu3 heoi3 dai6 ji6 dou6 lo2 seoi2

rows.note: Use an action verb such as 抹 or 吹 before 乾 to say that someone makes A dry.

example.english: I use a hairdryer to dry my hair.
example.jyutping: ngo5 jung6 fung1 tung2 ceoi1 gon1 tau4 faat3

rows.note: Use this for writing or subjects that are plain and unembellished, and by extension for something uninteresting.

example.english: This article is so dry that it makes you sleepy.
example.traditional: 呢篇文章寫得太平淡，睇到人想瞓覺。
example.jyutping: ni1 pin1 man4 zoeng1 se2 dak1 taai3 ping4 daam6 tai2 dou3 jan4 soeng2 fan3 gaau3

rows.note: Use this for drinks or products that contain no alcohol, rather than for a person abstaining from alcohol.

example.english: I bought a dry beer for my friend who was driving.
example.traditional: 我買咗枝無酒精啤酒畀揸車嘅朋友。
example.jyutping: ngo5 maai5 zo2 zi1 mou4 zau2 zing1 be1 zau2 bei2 zaa1 ce1 ge3 pang4 jau5

rows.note: Use this everyday description for wine or another drink that is unsweetened or low in sugar.

example.english: I like this white wine—it tastes dry.
example.traditional: 我鍾意呢款白酒，飲落唔甜。
example.jyutping: ngo5 zung1 ji3 ni1 fun2 baak6 zau2 jam2 lok6 m4 tim4
